//: Copy to server/sandbox.config.json (or set CCSERVER_SANDBOX_CONFIG) to customize the sandbox.
//docker: true (default): start an isolated rootless dockerd inside the sandbox. false: no docker (lighter, no rootlesskit). Ignored on macOS: sandbox-exec cannot host a nested dockerd, so macOS launches always run without docker (with a warning when this is true).
//persistentHome: true (default): keep a persistent writable HOME per project (under ~/.local/share/ccserver-sandbox/home/<project>) so tools/caches installed inside the sandbox survive a session relaunch. A launch dialog offers to reuse the previous sandbox or start fresh (which wipes that HOME). false: legacy fresh-tmpfs HOME every session.
//gpg: true: forward the host gpg-agent (bind ~/.gnupg + the live agent/keyboxd sockets) so commit signing works inside the sandbox using the host's key/token. Coexists with docker. Default false.
//gitBroker: true (default): git HTTPS/SSH access inside the sandbox is scoped to the repos actually related to the session (its own remotes + checked-out submodules, computed once at launch). `gh` is not disabled but rewired: gh invocations are relayed to the host broker, which executes a safelisted subset of subcommands for real (pr/issue/release/workflow/repo-view) against the same allow-list, and refuses everything else (gh api, gh auth, gh repo clone/fork/create, etc.) -- see README 'gh broker' for the exact list. No config needed for the common case -- this replaces the old approach of binding ~/.config/gh and ~/.ssh directly, which is no longer supported (those paths are never exposed, regardless of this flag or of `binds` below). Set false to turn off the broker/gate entirely (git still works, just unscoped if sshAgent is also on; gh runs unwrapped but has no credentials since ~/.config/gh stays blocked). NOT a hard boundary when docker:true (the default) AND sshAgent:true: a container started via `docker run` inside the sandbox doesn't inherit the ssh/gh wrappers and can mount the forwarded ssh-agent socket directly, bypassing the scoping. See README 'Known limitations'.
//commitMessageGuard: enabled: true (default): a `git commit` inside the sandbox whose message matches a blocked pattern is refused via a commit-msg hook (core.hooksPath, injected without touching ~/.gitconfig -- see commitGuard.js). Built-in patterns (always on, not listed here): a `Claude-Session:` trailer, and a bare `https://claude.ai/code/session_...` URL -- either would hand out live access to the conversation that produced the commit. Independent of gitBroker above (this is about local commit CONTENT, not network credential scope) -- it stays on even with gitBroker:false, and vice versa. blockedPatterns: [] (default) -- extra regex source strings (JS RegExp, compiled with flags 'im') to block in addition to the built-ins, e.g. a `Co-Authored-By: ... noreply@anthropic.com` trailer, which is deliberately NOT built in since many workflows want it kept. A pattern that fails to compile is logged and skipped, not fatal. Known limitation (same posture as gitBroker): `git commit --no-verify`, or a locally overridden `core.hooksPath`/`GIT_CONFIG_COUNT`, bypasses this entirely -- see README 'Known limitations'. When gitBroker is ALSO on, the same patterns are additionally checked against `gh pr create`/`edit`/`comment`/`review`'s title/body/--body-file (see ghAllowlist.js's extractGhTextFields + git-broker.js's findBlockedGhText) -- a git commit-msg hook never sees gh's own free-form PR text, so without this a `gh pr create --body "...Claude-Session: ..."` would sail straight through untouched. This gh-side check is unavailable with gitBroker:false (gh isn't broker-relayed at all then).
//forceSandbox: false (default): the client decides per session whether to run inside the sandbox (bwrap on Linux, sandbox-exec on macOS). true: forbid launching the agent or a shell outside the sandbox entirely -- every session is forced sandboxed, the per-session UI toggle is overridden, and a launch is REFUSED (instead of falling back to a direct unsandboxed spawn) when the sandbox is unavailable (bwrap not installed, sandbox-exec not available on macOS, or Windows). It also blocks the /usage background capture's direct-launch fallback. The sandbox backend (bwrap on Linux / sandbox-exec on macOS) must be available on the host for any session to start.
//sshAgent: true: forward the host's ssh-agent socket (auto-discovered, preferring one with keys loaded; override with env.SSH_AUTH_SOCK) into the sandbox as SSH_AUTH_SOCK. Only needed for SSH git remotes or running `ssh` directly inside the sandbox -- HTTPS git is already fully brokered by gitBroker without it, and commit signing is the separate gpg flag above. Default false: a forwarded agent is standing access to the host's real keys for the whole sandboxed process, not just git, so leave it off unless you actually need it. See README 'Known limitations' for the docker+gitBroker+sshAgent bypass.
//gpgVault: true: forward the MANAGED GPG vault agent's sockets instead of the host's own gpg-agent -- a different, passkey-login-only mechanism from the `gpg`/`sshAgent` flags above (see docs-site sandbox/credentials.md). The server holds a dedicated, server-generated GPG key, encrypted at rest, decryptable only via a live WebAuthn PRF ceremony against a registered passkey (Settings > GPG連携). Once unlocked, the managed gpg-agent signs commits (user.signingkey/commit.gpgsign/gpg.program injected automatically, alongside user.name/user.email matching the key's own UID) and serves as the SSH_AUTH_SOCK for `git push` over SSH, via gpg-agent's own SSH-agent emulation. A launch requesting this while the vault is locked or never set up is REFUSED (not silently degraded) -- unlock it from Settings first. Only meaningful with CCSERVER_AUTH_MODE=passkey; ignored otherwise. Default false. See gpgVaultLockPolicy below for the vault's own auto-lock policy -- a separate, lifecycle-level setting under its OWN top-level key (not nested under this boolean, which would collide shapes).
//gpgVaultLockPolicy: idleTimeoutMinutes: 0 (default, disabled) -- the GPG vault auto-locks only when every browser session has expired (bound to auth_sessions' own 30-day sliding TTL) -- deliberately NOT a short idle timer, since this server runs long, unattended, autonomous agent sessions that would otherwise have signing/pushing broken mid-task with no human present to re-unlock. Set a positive integer to additionally enforce a hard wall-clock TTL (minutes since the vault was last unlocked, not true activity detection) for operators who want a stricter leash despite that tradeoff. Read independently by gpgVaultAgent.js, not part of the per-session sandbox options above.
//tools: Opt-in tools provisioned INTO the sandbox HOME at launch, so nothing has to be pre-installed on the host OS (see README 'Sandbox tool provisioning'). Keys: "rtk" (Rust Token Killer CLI proxy, static binary from GitHub releases) and "code-review-graph" (graph MCP + CLI via a pip venv). Each accepts true (= a pinned default version) or an object to override fields (e.g. { "version": "v0.45.0", "url": "...", "sha256": "..." } for rtk; { "version": "2.3.7" } for code-review-graph). Installation is idempotent (a version marker under the sandbox HOME skips already-provisioned tools), so a persistent HOME only pays the install cost once -- a new/wipe launch re-provisions from scratch. Requires network from inside the sandbox on first install, and python3+venv present on the host (the sandbox binds /usr). The client's launch menu offers the same per-session toggle, remembered per directory; this config is the server-wide fallback for clients that don't send a per-session choice. Default here: off.
//tools-note: SECURITY: the pinned rtk sha256 covers x64 only; on other arches the checksum is skipped (with a terminal warning) unless you pin "sha256" explicitly in the object form. Pin it when running non-x64 hosts.
//binds: Extra host paths exposed inside the sandbox, on top of the project dir + ~/.claude + ~/.claude.json (and, with gpg:true, ~/.gnupg). mode: 'ro' (default) or 'rw'. Missing sources are skipped. ~ expands to your home. ~/.ssh and ~/.config/gh are always blocked here (see gitBroker above), so don't list them.
//env: Extra environment variables set inside the sandbox (applied last, so they override defaults). e.g. force a specific SSH_AUTH_SOCK.
//claudeBin: How to launch claude. Default: auto — resolve 'claude' on PATH and, if it's a wrapper to the real binary (e.g. /usr/bin/claude -> /opt/claude-code/bin/claude), expose that install dir in the sandbox automatically. Set this only if claude lives somewhere the auto-detect misses, or to pin a specific build. Absolute path recommended. Env var CCSERVER_CLAUDE_BIN overrides this. (opencode, copilot and codex are auto-resolved from PATH/~/.opencode/bin and ~/.local/bin respectively; command-code additionally searches project .tools/bin for command-code/commandcode/cmdc/cmd; there is no per-app bin setting for them.)
//defaultApp: Which agent CLI a new session launches when the client doesn't request one (legacy scheduled prompts, or a browser tab that hasn't picked one yet). 'claude' (default), 'opencode', 'copilot', 'codex' or 'commandcode'. The launch UI's own choice (remembered per browser) always wins once made; this only seeds that choice on first load and covers server-side fallback paths. Combo (group) members never use it — groups default to claude and refuse copilot/commandcode.
//showUsage: true (default): the client shows the top-bar Usage button (Claude Code /usage spend). false: hide it entirely. The button is also hidden automatically when claude is not installed on this server (the /usage capture could never succeed).
//opencodeGoUsage: true (default): show the OpenCode Go tab in the Usage popover (quota from https://opencode.ai/zen/go/v1/usage, authenticated with the Go API key opencode itself stores in ~/.local/share/opencode/auth.json). An opencode CLI install alone says nothing about a Go subscription, so this is a separate toggle: false hides the tab entirely (no key is read, no request is sent). When on, the tab is still auto-hidden while no Go key exists, and a key without a subscription shows a 'no subscription' message instead of numbers. Env var CCSERVER_OPENCODE_GO_USAGE (0/false/off/no or 1/true/on/yes) wins over this file.
//hiddenApps: [] (default): agent CLI ids ('claude', 'opencode', 'copilot', 'codex') to remove entirely from every launch picker (single-launch modal, combo role pickers, worker preset management, meta-agent launch, the Usage button's app tabs) -- e.g. CLIs installed on this host but that you haven't actually contracted for. Unlike an app the server just can't find (still shown greyed out with a 'サーバーに未インストール' tooltip), a hidden app never appears at all; there is no partial/greyed hide mode. Unknown entries are ignored. The server refuses to start if this hides every agent CLI actually installed here (nothing would be launchable) -- leave at least one selectable. Also enforced server-side at createSession(), not just in the pickers: a hidden app is refused for every new-session path (direct WS/REST calls, worker/launch-preset expansion, meta-agent MCP tools, scheduled-prompt auto-resume), so hiding one is a real restriction, not just a UI convenience.
//usageMcp: false (default): do not inject the ccserver-usage get_usage MCP into Claude sessions. Set true to opt in. This is independent of the Usage button above.
//metaAgentMcp: false (default): do not host the ccserver-meta MCP broker. Set true to opt in. ccserver-meta is a PRIVILEGED server-management toolset (list/launch/close sessions, launch/destroy groups, delete sandboxes, manage presets and project labels); destructive calls additionally require human approval through a browser banner dialog before they run. When enabled, the toolset is injected ONLY into a session explicitly launched with isMetaAgent:true (e.g. POST /api/sessions with isMetaAgent:true) -- never into regular sessions or group members. Such sessions are always forced into the fixed project-outside directory ~/.local/share/ccserver-sandbox/meta-agent (client cwd is ignored) and started via the dedicated "⌘ メタエージェント" button.
//reviewerMcp: false (default): do not host the ccserver-reviewer MCP broker. Set true to opt in. run_review launches a disposable headless session against a fresh, throwaway git worktree (never the caller's own cwd) and drives it through /code-review, for a local ref/branch/PR/uncommitted diff. Unlike ccserver-meta, it is injected into ANY session -- shells and copilot excluded, groups/workers included -- since reviewing code needs no special privilege beyond spawning a sandboxed session. Job status/results are queryable via list_reviews/get_review and persist in the SQLite pr_reviews table across a restart.
//notify: ccserver-notify MCP (通知用, 下記 README)。discordWebhook: https:// の Discord webhook URL (空文字で無効)。設定するとエージェントの notify ツールが Discord へ通知を送れる。CCSERVER_DISCORD_WEBHOOK 環境変数で上書き可。subscriptions: 初期購読 (bootstrap)。https:// の webhook URL の配列。購読ゼロかつ discordWebhook 未設定かつ vikunja 未設定なら MCP は注入されない。hostname: 通知フッターのホスト名を固定したい場合のみ (未設定なら OS の hostname、CCSERVER_HOSTNAME 環境変数が最優先)。attribution: false にすると通知ペイロード末尾の "_from: host · project · group · session" フッターを丸ごと無効化 (既定 true)。

notify.//vikunja: notify 呼び出しごとに Vikunja タスクを作成/更新する (Discord/webhook と並行配信、失敗してもエージェント側にはエラーを返さない)。baseUrl (https:// のみ) と apiToken の両方が設定されていれば有効になり、Discord/購読が空でも notify MCP 自体が注入される。apiToken は秘匿値なので、ここに書く代わりに環境変数 CCSERVER_VIKUNJA_API_TOKEN 経由を強く推奨 (sandbox.config.json は .gitignore 済みだが、それでも平文保存はできるだけ避ける)。baseUrl は CCSERVER_VIKUNJA_BASE_URL、projectId は CCSERVER_VIKUNJA_PROJECT_ID で上書き可。projectId 未設定だとタスク作成は行われない (warning ログのみ)。timeoutSeconds (既定15秒) はリクエストごとのタイムアウト。verifyTls: false で自己署名証明書のインスタンスを許容 (既定 true、無闇に false にしない)。statusLabelPrefix はラベル名の prefix (既定 'status-')。buckets.doing/buckets.todo は Kanban バケット名 (既定 'Doing'/'To-Do')。Claude が作業中 (level: info) は buckets.doing へ、それ以外 (success/warning/error、= 人間の番) は buckets.todo へタスクを移動する。無ければ自動作成する。CCSERVER_VIKUNJA_BUCKET_DOING / CCSERVER_VIKUNJA_BUCKET_TODO で上書き可。タスクを done (完了) にする操作は行わない -- 人間が Vikunja 上で確認して手動で done にする運用。

//federation: 拠点間ペアリング (下記 README「拠点間 (federation) ペアリング」)。requireTokenForPairing: true にすると、ペアリング開始リクエスト (bootstrap) にだけこのインスタンスの CCSERVER_TOKEN の提示を必須にする (既定 false)。あくまでスパム対策で、トークンが合っていても双方向の人間承認は省略されない。機能自体の有効/無効はここではなく CCSERVER_FEDERATION_PORT 環境変数で制御する。
//network: ネットワーク分離。isolate: 機能全体のon/off (既定 false=無効)。false ではいずれのバックエンドでもブローカーを起動せず、従来通り open egress で起動する (稼働中トグル自体が現れない)。true でのみブローカー起動＋境界を張る (Linux: 私有netns/ファイアウォール、macOS: broker-onlyプロファイル)。initialState: 隔離を有効にして起動したセッションの開始state ('enforce'既定 または 'open'。稼働中の 🌐 トグルでいつでも切替でき、再起動不要、この切替は sandbox.config.json を書き換えない。open時も直結TCP/UDPは不可でproxy経由のみ -- proxyを無視するツールはopenでも直結できない)。mode: 'enforce'(既定、許可外をブロック) または 'audit'(ブロックせず判定のみログに記録。ただし deniedHosts は audit でも貫徹する)。allowedHosts: 完全一致 または 先頭ドット(サブドメイン込み、例 '.example.com')のみ受け付ける -- scheme・ポート・ワイルドカードは不可、最大200件。deniedHosts: 同じ記法の絶対拒否リストで、allow-list・live open state・audit モードすべてに優先する(最大200件)。allowedHosts/deniedHosts の保存は稼働中の分離済みセッションへ自動反映される(isolate/initialState/mode の変更は次回起動から)。bwrap は rootlesskit/slirp4netns/newuidmap が揃っているホストでのみ isolate:true を実際に有効化できる(揃っていないホストでは isolate:true でも従来通り非隔離で起動し、警告ログを出す)。seatbelt にこのツール依存はない。どちらのバックエンドも defense-in-depth (bwrap はカーネルレベルの netns+ファイアウォールで構造的、seatbelt は同一UIDプロセスからの KERN_PROCARGS2 経由のトークン読み取りを防げないためプロファイルレベルのみ)。
